title: Squeeze both release buttons and slide the battery off the drill
instruction: Hold the drill with the right hand. With the left hand, squeeze both release buttons on the orange battery, slide the battery off the drill's handle and put it in the blue tray.
context: E-waste recyclers take the lithium battery out of every cordless tool before shredding it. The pack is locked on until both release buttons are squeezed at once, and it slides off against the grip of its rails, so one hand holds the tool while the other squeezes and pulls.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Drill: a cordless 18 V drill/driver (22.5 cm long, 22.8 cm tall with its pack, 5.8 cm wide), green and black plastic with a steel chuck, 1.2 kg without its battery, lying loose on its left side with its handle pointing toward the robot along x and its chuck pointing right. Its bounding box runs from x = 0.20 to 0.38 and y = -0.09 to 0.14 (centre (0.29, 0.02)), the motor housing across the far end, the handle's foot nearest the robot. Battery pack: an orange 18 V pack, 7 cm across its buttons (along y), 5 cm along the handle (along x), 5.8 cm thick (as thick as the drill lies), 450 g, seated on the handle's foot at (0.176, 0.056), 2.9 cm up. It slides off along the handle toward the robot: 4 cm of travel against 10 N of friction, then it is free. It is locked on until both release buttons are pressed at the same time. Release buttons: two black 1 cm square buttons, one in the middle of each face across the pack (facing left and right), standing 3 mm proud, 3 mm of travel, 5 N springs. The lock lets go while both are 1.5 mm or more in, and clicks back if they are let go with the pack within 2 mm of its seat. Tray: a blue plastic parts tray, 20 x 15 cm (20 cm along x), 8 mm walls 4 cm high, 6 mm floor, fixed on the robot's left at (0.19, 0.25). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Positions are centres. The pack's seat is where it sits on the handle's foot, wherever the drill now lies. Both buttons count as pressed together once both have been 1.5 mm or more in at the same control step, and this is remembered. 0 if the drill or the pack falls off the table (centre more than 2 cm below the table top). Every score above 0 needs both buttons pressed together at some step. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): the pack off the drill (its centre 5 cm or more from its seat), its centre within 8 cm along x and 5.5 cm along y of the tray's centre and less than 6 cm above the tray floor, the pack still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), and the drill's centre within 10 cm of its start (in the plane of the table). 0.5: the pack off the drill but not lying still in the tray, or in the tray with the drill moved 10 cm or more. 0.25: the pack slid 1 cm or more along the handle, still on the drill. 0 otherwise, including doing nothing, squeezing without sliding, and dragging the drill along with its pack.
reset_notes: Slide the battery back onto the handle's foot until it clicks, lay the drill back in its place and empty the tray.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The drill is NVIDIA's SimReady model, one rigid body colliding as its mesh, its moulded-on pack removed. The pack and the tray collide as boxes (the meshes are drawn only). The pack slides on a joint with a 10 N friction drive and a lock switched by a step hook, the buttons are sprung joints. Gripper 50 N per pad. Masses are typical values.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms reach the drill and nudge it, but it never squeezes the two buttons or slides the battery), demo: 1.0 (success at step 257)
